release_notes: Build 95 fixes the shared C: project-path blocker shown by Archive completed C by detecting Quiz History rows that incorrectly point at the same physical project folder.

Before archiving, Factburst identifies the single History row that best belongs to each shared C: folder using video type, series/title/category metadata, project files, and episode evidence; the corrupt stored path itself is excluded from the matching score.

Folders such as 'General Knowledge Quiz - 002' can use the trailing 002 as episode evidence, while folders with an explicit marker such as 'Film Quiz #002 - Short - 001' continue to use #002 and do not mistake the final 001 for the episode.

Other rows sharing that C: folder are offered only unique High-confidence one-to-one C:/Z: path repairs. Duplicate repair changes Quiz History database paths only and never moves, copies, overwrites, renames, or deletes project files.

After duplicate-path repair, Factburst rescans the database. Archive completed C proceeds only when the shared links are gone; unresolved or ambiguous rows remain untouched and block deletion of the affected C: folder.
Update paths now preserves valid one-to-one paths and refuses discovered matches when more than one History row would claim the same project folder.

A database update trigger also prevents future path-update operations from assigning a folder that is already linked to another Quiz History row, while still allowing existing duplicate rows to be repaired away from the shared path.
Build 94's faster archive preview and live x-of-y C: to Z: copy/verify progress window remain in place, and existing Z: folders are still never overwritten or deleted.
